newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks jump on heavy volume in morning.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks jump on heavy volume in morning.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks rose sharply in Monday morning trade, with the Hang Seng index coming close to its 1996 high before easing off slightly, following record high levels hit by Wall Street stocks on Friday.
The Hang Seng index was up 157.08 points, or 1.38 percent, at 11,526.12 after hitting an early high 11,584.27. This was just shy of the 1996 high of 11,600.
Turnover was a heavy HK$2.25 billion after 50 minutes of trade.
"It's powering ahead," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.

The Dow industrials rose 66.58 points on Friday to close at a record high of 5,838.52, after U.S. consumer price data showed a 0.1 percent rise in the August consumer price index compared with expectations of a 0.2 percent rise.
The U.S. long bond surged 1-15/32 to yield 6.95 percent.
Analysts said recent U.S. economic data suggested the Federal Reserve may not have to raise interest rates in the short term.

"Right now the economic data suggest inflation is quite moderate so I expect the Fed to leave rates unchanged and they won't have to raise them until December," said Ricky Tam, senior research analyst at Delta Asia Securities.

Analysts said the Hang Seng was likely to meet some resistance around the 11,600 area. "I think the main resistance is 11,600. That resistance level is the long term uptrend line from January 1995 to now," said Tam.
He said if the Hang Seng index breaks through 11,600 points, the next target was 12,000.

Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales at Standard Chartered, said there was a lot of momentum from overseas markets boosting local shares but he did not expect much more upside this session. Shares in Frankfurt and London hit records on Friday.
"It will not go much higher today. I see it gradually moving up during the week," said Galbraith.
Shares in HSBC Holdings rose HK$2.00 to HK$139.50 and Henderson Land was up HK$1.25 at HK$64.75.
